item.title: Cardiometabolic Treatments, Rare Diseases, Variable Dosing, and Quanta | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Bart Burgess discusses some of the key areas for innovation in the industry, such as rare diseases and moving away from variable dosing solutions, and introduces Quanta – SHL's latest product offering.

item.title: Sustainable Packaging and Patient-Centric Design | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Steve Augustyn and Jon Powell discuss a range of key topics in the drug delivery industry, including design complexity, sustainable materials and patient-centric design.

item.title: ADDRESSING OCULAR SAFETY CHALLENGES IN ADC DEVELOPMENT | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Dr Tina Rogers discusses antibody-drug conjugates and their potential in direct targeting and treatment of cancers, going further to assess the risks of these treatments and how they can be mitigated.

item.title: INTRAVITREAL INJECTIONS – WHAT IS CAUSING PATIENTS TO DISCONTINUE THERAPY AND WHY IS IT SO HARD TO FIX? | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Gregg Draudt considers the significant issue of treatment discontinuation in intravitreal therapies, digging into the root causes of poor adherence and what will be required to reverse this trend in a way that caters to the full range of stakeholders, who often have contradictory requirements.

item.title: NOVELIA®: ENABLING THE NEXT GENERATION OF PRESERVATIVE-FREE MULTIDOSE OPHTHALMICS | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Severine Duband and Natalia Zabala discuss the role of multidose preservative-free eyedroppers in the ophthalmic market, highlighting the advantages of Nemera’s Novelia® platform, including its non-return valve system, the sustainability of multidose delivery and the platform’s growing success within the Chinese market.

item.title: EMPOWERING VISION FOR THE FUTURE: ADVANCED CONTAINMENT SOLUTIONS FOR OPHTHALMIC APPLICATIONS | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Dr Linara Cornell, Dr Manali Potnis and Dr Krishnendu Khan review the current landscape and challenges associated with delivery systems for ophthalmic applications, and how West Pharmaceutical Services plays a critical role in this specialised industry by providing high quality prefilled syringe components and systems that meet the stringent requirements for these sight-saving therapies.

item.title: SHL MEDICAL AND BAYER: A COLLABORATIVE APPROACH TO ADVANCING INTRAVITREAL PAEDIATRIC DOSING | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Andreas Kalitzki, Samuel Wyler and Seda Aksel explain how Bayer and SHL Medical collaborative efforts are enhancing paediatric intravitreal injections through evidence-based dosing strategies and clinically validated therapies using SHL Medical’s Micro Dosing Device technology.

item.title: THE CHALLENGES IN DEVELOPING AND MANUFACTURING CUSTOM OPHTHALMIC INJECTOR DEVICES | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Dr Lorna Barron sets out the standards that must be met for effective drug delivery to the eye, characterising both old and new delivery routes that may be used to address the unique challenges of ophthalmic disease.

item.title: THE RETINAL DELIVERY BOTTLENECK: WHY TODAY’S TOOLS WON’T SCALE | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: Dr David Cottenden and Benjamin Hatton examine the rapid shift towards cell and gene therapies in ophthalmology, indicated by current pharmaceutical pipelines, and reveal a potential delivery crisis – today’s surgical capacity cannot support what the pipeline demands. Considering this, they explore why a radical rethink of retinal delivery tools could unlock scalable access to the retina.

item.title: MY STERINITY NASAL PLATFORM: A PRODUCT OF COLLABORATION - LAUNCHING AT DCAT WEEK | ONdrugDelivery
item.description: SGD Pharma discusses the advantages and benefits of the company’s recent partnership with Prince Sterilization Services, with a focus on the first product platform developed based on this collaboration – the My Sterinity Nasal platform of Type I glass primary containers for sensitive, long-term nasal therapeutics. Additionally, SGD Pharma highlights its presence at DCAT Week 2026.
